$comment: Neutral description of the Duet 3 CAN message formats. This file is the single source of truth;
(C#) are generated from it by src/DuetCanMessage.SourceGenerators.
Layout rules (verified against g++ __attribute__((packed)) on little-endian targets):
- a bit cursor runs through the struct; a bitfield is placed at the cursor and advances it by its
width, with no padding and no regard for the declared storage type (bitfields may straddle both
byte and storage-unit boundaries, and consecutive groups of different storage types pack together);
- a non-bitfield member rounds the cursor up to the next byte boundary before being placed;
- the struct size is the cursor rounded up to a whole number of bytes.
Field order therefore matters and must not be changed without bumping the message type.

cppHeaders.name: CanMessageFormats.h
preamble: // Some messages end in strings. For such messages, it is safe to compute the message length without allowing for a null terminator,
// because when our sending functions round the message length up to a supported CAN size the additional data is set to zeros.
// All fields named 'zero' are spare and must be set to 0 for compatibility with future uses.
// Message formats that take a request ID have a SetRequestId method that sets the request ID and clears the zero fields.
// Message formats that don't take a request ID have a ClearReservedFields method that clears the zero fields.

constantGroups.name: StandardDriverStatus

Only the lowest 16 bits travel in a driver event message.
